title: Show the night team's overtime balance the way payroll reads it

blocks.text: A care home pays its staff for the hours they work beyond their contract, and deducts the hours they fall short. Payslips show the week's balance as hours and minutes: `2:30` over, `-0:40` short. Since the night team joined, payroll has seen a full week of nights shown as dozens of hours short, a balance printed as `0:-40`, and a nurse who worked a week of double shifts shown as only a few hours over.
`Timesheet.balance(...)` already adds up the shifts and subtracts the contract. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Timesheet.java`:

items: `length(start, end)`: how long one shift lasts, given the times on the clock;
`label(amount)`: the text payroll reads, hours then a colon and two-digit minutes, with a minus sign in front when the amount is negative.

cases.says: a week of day shifts gives the hours and two-digit minutes worked beyond the contract
a shift whose end on the clock is before its start ends the next day and counts every hour it lasted
a balance of more than 24 hours shows all its hours, not only those past the last whole day
a negative balance shows one minus sign in front and positive two-digit minutes

origin.section: Duration Prints Hours, Not Days, and Its Hours and Minutes Carry the Sign

concepts: Duration.between two LocalTimes subtracts, so a span past midnight comes out negative unless a day is added.
toHours() is the total hours while toHoursPart() is the hours left after whole days.
The hours, minutes and seconds parts of a negative Duration are all negative, so a label is built from the sign once and the parts of abs().
